title: Where Locals Linger: 10 Places to Sit for Hours
description: Ten Moscow setups built for unhurried time: reading rooms with desks and power, quiet coworking spaces, and parks furnished with benches, tables, shade, and loungers.

cards.title: Zaryadye Park
cards.subtitle: Hundreds of benches threaded through the park’s landscape zones
cards.notes: Wide resting steps, illuminated seats, and oak-and-stone benches line the central paths. The city’s project page describes free, round-the-clock park access; individual attractions may operate separately.
cards.short_summary: Follow the paths until the view and the right-shaped bench line up.
cards.source_title: Парк «Зарядье» — Комплекс градостроительной политики и строительства города Москвы

cards.title: Green River Park
cards.subtitle: Tables under a canopy, loungers, hammocks, and a covered public room
cards.notes: The Lefortovo section includes four tables with benches beneath a pergola and ten loungers on sand. A larger roofed area adds hammocks, game tables, and amphitheater seating for weather-resistant pauses.
cards.short_summary: Bring a book to the pergola, or move under the larger roof when the weather turns.
cards.source_title: Анастасия Пятова: Завершен новый участок парка «Зелёная река» в Лефортове

cards.title: Russian State Library
cards.subtitle: Thirty-four reading rooms with more than 1,600 seats
cards.notes: A reader pass opens a substantial choice of desks, specialized rooms, computer access, and reader areas. The library says Russian and foreign citizens aged 14 or older can obtain a pass with identification.
cards.short_summary: Choose the room by subject, then settle into one of the library’s many formal work seats.
cards.source_title: Visit the Library — Russian State Library

cards.entity_name: State Public Historical Library of Russia
cards.title: State Public Historical Library of Russia
cards.subtitle: An 80-seat reading hall with laptop-equipped places
cards.notes: The main hall combines long-form desk work with more than 10,000 open-shelf volumes. Registration is required; the library publishes separate registration and reading-room schedules.
cards.short_summary: A practical desk-and-laptop room when the day’s subject is history—or simply sustained concentration.
cards.source_title: Читальные залы — Государственная публичная историческая библиотека России

cards.entity_name: Russian State Library for Young Adults
cards.title: Russian State Library for Young Adults
cards.subtitle: Reading tables with power sockets and library-wide Wi-Fi
cards.notes: Every reading table has an electrical outlet for personal laptops. The building also offers open Wi-Fi, public computers, subject rooms, a study room, and an armchair listening setup for audiobooks.
cards.short_summary: A plugged-in library day with several rooms to change pace without leaving the building.
cards.source_title: Технологии — Российская государственная библиотека для молодежи

cards.entity_name: Miguel Delibes Library at Instituto Cervantes Moscow
cards.title: Miguel Delibes Library at Instituto Cervantes Moscow
cards.subtitle: Nineteen work seats in a quiet reading room open to all visitors
cards.notes: Most of the Spanish-language collection is open-shelf, and three computers handle audio and video materials. The library asks readers to keep conversations quiet and leave finished books on the tables or collection cart.
cards.short_summary: A small, clearly structured room for reading Spanish-language books at a proper desk.
cards.source_title: Читальный зал в библиотеке — Институт Сервантеса в Москве

cards.title: Pushkin Library Family Reading Department
cards.subtitle: Separate coworking and computer-work spaces for different age groups
cards.notes: This branch at 16 Bolshaya Pochtovaya divides its ground floor into children’s, youth, and adult sectors. Alongside the work areas are rooms for games, lectures, screenings, and workshops; consult the branch-specific schedule before going.
cards.short_summary: Pick the age-appropriate sector, then use the dedicated coworking setup instead of improvising at a café table.
cards.source_title: Библиотека-читальня им. А.С. Пушкина — официальный сайт

cards.title: Nikolay Dobrolyubov Library
cards.subtitle: Reading rooms configured as an adult coworking space
cards.notes: The library explicitly pairs its reading rooms with Wi-Fi and access to the National Electronic Library and LitRes. Reader registration is available on site; non-Russian residents are directed to register in person.
cards.short_summary: A conventional reading room with the network access needed for a longer research session.
cards.source_title: Посетителям библиотеки — Библиотека имени Н.А. Добролюбова, Музей Москвы

cards.title: Library No. 41, Kuusinena Street Branch
cards.subtitle: A reading room with Wi-Fi, public computers, newspapers, and magazines
cards.notes: The Northern Administrative District’s official cultural network lists the specific setup at 6 Kuusinena Street, Building 6. It is a straightforward branch option for desk work or a long pass through current periodicals.
cards.short_summary: Come for a computer or Wi-Fi; stay at the reading-room desk with the newspaper rack nearby.

cards.entity_name: Rudomino All-Russia State Library for Foreign Literature
cards.title: Rudomino Library for Foreign Literature
cards.subtitle: Two levels of reading space plus smaller study rooms
cards.notes: The library’s visitor directions map a lower and upper tier, a small reading room, a document-issue hall, and several language and cultural centers. The published reading-room schedule extends through the day; registration requirements should be checked before arrival.
cards.short_summary: Start in the two-level reading hall, then shift to a smaller room when you need a tighter focus.
